chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, with an unbroken chain going up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The fever goes out (is cured) in three ways: through sweating, through the belly (excretion), and through vomiting.
ai.seo_question: What are the three ways fever is cured according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies fever (al-humma) as a natural divine mechanism that expels impurities through three primary channels: perspiration, bowel movements, and vomiting. This narration reflects the classical Islamic medical understanding of humoral theory, where fever is viewed not merely as a symptom but as an active therapeutic process initiated by God to restore bodily balance.

en.hubeali: H 14858 – From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid with an unbroken chain going up to Abu Abdullahasws, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws having said:
‘The fever goes out (is cured) in three (ways) – The sweating, and the excretion and the vomiting’.
en.sarwar: 411. From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid with an unbroken chain going up to Abu Abdullah (a.s.), who has narrated the following:
Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said: ‘The fever goes out (is cured) in three (ways) – The sweating, and the excretion and the vomiting’.
